t: If the emf of an AC source is given by 6sinωt+4sin2ωt V, then the rms value of the emf is

Given, emf of an AC source,
[  E=6sinωt+4sin2ωt; Now,  E²=(6sinωt+4sin2ωt)²; ∴E²=36sin²2ωt+16sin²2ωt+48sinωt⋅sin2ωt; =36sin²ωt+16sin²2ωt+48(cosωt/2−cos3ωt/2)]
Now, the average value of E²,
[ ∴ E_(avg)=1/T∫_0^T [E²dt]; =1/T∫_0^T [36sin²ωt+16sin²2ωt+48(cosωt/2−cos3ωt/2)]; =1/T[36⋅T/2+16×T/2+48(0−0)]; or  E_(avg)=18+8=26 V; ∴ Eᵣₘₛ=√(E_(avg))=√26 V; ]

t: An ac source of angular frequency ω is fed across a resistor R and a capacitor C in series. The current in the circuit is I. If now the frequency of source is changed to ω/3 (but maintaining the same voltage), the current in the circuit is found to be halved. s:
At angular frequency ω, the current in RC circuit is given by
iₘₐₓ=Vₘₐₓ/(√(R²+(1/ωC)²)) …….(i)
Also iᵣₘₛ/2=Vᵣₘₛ/(√(R²+(1/(ω/3C))²))=Vₘₐₓ/(√(R²+9/ω²C²)) …….(ii)
From equation (i) and (ii) we get
3R²=5/ω²C²⇒(1/ωC)/R=√(3/5)⇒X_C/R=√(3/5)

t: An AC source of angular frequency ω is fed across a resistor R and a capacitor C in series. The current flowing in the circuit found to be I. Now the frequency of the source is changed to ω/3, (maintaining the same voltage) the current in the circuit is found to be halved. What is the ratio of reactance to resistance at the original frequency?
s:
At angular frequency ω, current through resistance R and capacitance C is given by
Iᵣₘₛ=Vᵣₘₛ/(√(R²+X_C²))=Vᵣₘₛ/(√(R²+(1/ωC)²))…(i)
When angular frequency is changed to ω/3, then the current becomes
Iᵣₘₛ/2=Vᵣₘₛ/(√(R²+(1/(ω/3C))²))=Vᵣₘₛ/(√(R²+(3/ωC)²))...(ii)
Dividing Eq. (i) by Eq. (ii), we get
[2=(√(R²+(3/ωC)²))/(√(R²+(1/ωC)²)); ⇒4[R²+(1/ωC)²]=R²+(3/ωC)²; ⇒3R²=5/ω²C²; ⇒1/(X_C/R)=√(3/5); ⇒X_C/R=√(3/5)]

t:
A square frame with side ’ a^′ and a straight conductor carrying current I are located in the same plane. The inductance and the resistance of the frame are equal to L and R respectively. The frame was turned through 180° about the axis OO’ separated from the current carrying conductor by a distance b. What is the electric charge flown through the frame?
[[img:6af34d56d5d6]]
s:
According to ohm’s law and Faraday’s law of induction, the current i₀ appearing the frame during its rotation is determined by the formula i₀=dϕ/dt=−Ldi₀/dt Hence, the required amount of electric charge is
q=∫i₀dt=−1/R∫(dϕ+Ldi₀)
=1/R∫(Δϕ+LΔi₀)
Where R is the resistance and L is the inductance of the frame. Since the frame has been stopped after rotation, the current in it vanishes eventually. Therefore Δi₀=0. It remains for us to find the increment of the flux Δϕ through the frame (Δϕ=ϕ₂−ϕ₁). Let us choose the normal n̂ to the plane of the frame such that in the final position, n̂ is directed perpendicular to the plane and towards it. Then it can easily seen that in the final position ϕ₂>0. While in the initial position ϕ₁>0 and Δϕ turns out to be simply equal to the flux through the surface bounded by the final and initial positions of the frame:
Δϕ=ϕ₂−(−ϕ₁)=∫_(b−a)^(b+a) Badr
Where B is a function of r, whose form can be easily found with the help of the Ampere’s circuital law or Biot-Savart law. Finally, we obtain q=Δϕ/R=μ₀aI/2πRIn((b+a)/(b−a))

t: A motor having an armature of resistance 2Ω is designed to operate at 220 V mains. At full speed, it develops a back e.m.f. of 210 V. What is the current in the armature when the motor is running at full speed?
s:
Rₐ=2Ω,Eₐ=220 V,E_b=210 V. Current at full speed is
Iₐ=(Eₐ−E_b)/Rₐ=(220−210)/2=5A

t: An LCR series circuit with R=100Ω is connected to a 200 V,50 Hz a.c. source. When only the capacitance is removed, the voltage leads the current by 60°. When only the inductance is removed, the current leads the voltage by 60°. The current in the circuit is
s:
When capacitance is removed, the circuit contains only inductance and resistance. Phase difference θ between the current and voltage is then given by
tanθ=ωL/R or ωL=Rtanθ=100tan60°
When the circuit contains only capacitance and resistance, the phase difference between the voltage and current is given by tanϕ=1/RCω
∴ 1/Cω=Rtanϕ=100tan60°
The impedance of the LCR circuit is given by
Z=√(R²+(ωL−1/Cω)²)=√(R²+(100tan60°−100tan60°)²)=R=100Ω
The current is given by
I=V/R=200/100=2 A

t:

[[img:e06447534244]]
s:
V(t)=(4V₀/T)t  for 0≤t≤T/4
∴ ⟨V²⟩_(0−T/4)=((16V₀²/T²)∫_0^(T/4) t²dt)/(∫_0^(T/4) dt)=V₀²/3
V²=(16V²/T²)t²
